scope: value-to-length curve, first four points: constant 55 bits up to 1024, then 97 at 5830
what_the_curve_shows: the cost is CONSTANT at 55 bits for 256, 512 and 1024 - three different bit lengths (9, 10, 11), so the cost is not bit-length driven in that range
so there is a threshold somewhere between 1024 and 5830, and crossing it adds a large fixed amount (about 42 bits) rather than a gradual growth
interpretation: a 42-bit jump looks like an extra structured field being decoded (e.g. a second value, or a 32-bit payload plus a few flags), not a length prefix
and because 256/512/1024 are all equal, the encoder is treating those as 'small' values in a fixed slot
next: bisect the threshold: 2048 and 4096 are the natural candidates (11 and 12 bits)
then, once the threshold is known, test a value just below and just above it to confirm the jump is a step and not a slope
